headline: Acceptance-aware training improves reported speculative-decoding acceptance length in matched regimes
summary: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces expected-accepted-length (EAL) training for greedy verification and window-total-variation (WTV) training for sampling-based speculative decoding. Across author-run Qwen3 and Gemma4 configurations and five benchmarks, the authors report higher mean acceptance lengths for matched objectives, with larger gains under sampling than greedy verification. In Qwen3-8B/Qwen3-0.6B tree decoding, WTV raises reported mean acceptance length from 4.998 to 5.750 at temperature 1.0 and from 4.304 to 4.780 at 0.5; under greedy verification, KL+EAL changes 4.494 to 4.503 while WTV alone is weaker at 4.428. The paper measures acceptance length, not end-to-end latency or serving cost. These results are claimed by the preprint authors and have not been independently reproduced.
